news.title: "He thrives with extra responsibility": South Africa fielding coach backs Rickelton ahead of Gqeberha Test
news.og_desc: Following a heavy 214-run defeat to Australia in the opening Test of the ICC World Test Championship series in Durban, South Africa are looking to make key adjustments as they prepare for the second match in Gqeberha. One of the major changes is Ryan Rickelton's return to wicketkeeping duties, a move the team's coaching staff believes could increase his involvement in the game, as per the ICC website. South Africa fielding coach Kruger van Wyk expressed confidence in Rickelton's transition behind the stumps, stating that the batter has continued to hone his wicketkeeping skills despite not regularly taking on the role. When we take the early bus, Ricks always comes along. Even when he doesn't keep in matches, he still comes and does his work, Kruger van Wyk, the former New Zealand wicketkeeper, who is now South Africa's fielding coach, was quoted by Cricinfo in Gqeberha ahead of the second Test against Australia. He is diligent with his work. Even when he just plays as a batter, in the white-ball stuff as well, he does his keeping work as well. So it's not like he's had to dust them [his keeping pads and gloves] off and start over again, he said. Van Wyk expressed complete confidence in Rickelton's technical abilities and readiness for the red-ball international arena, drawing comparisons to his exploits in franchise leagues. I think he's a first-choice keeper, van Wyk said. He has kept unbelievably well. And if you follow white-ball cricket, and his performances in IPL, you know it's still a ball coming down at you. It's still cricket. The movements are the same. The way you glove it is exactly the same. Technically, he is very good. While conditions in South Africa present different challenges compared to turning tracks abroad, van Wyk pointed out that Rickelton's prior experience keeping to elite global talent prepares him well for the assignment. He's not going to get tested as much in South Africa with spin, where the real test will come in the subcontinent - Sri Lanka, going forward, van Wyk said. In South African conditions, the ball bounces more than it spins. We saw a bit of spin in Durban, but it's not excessive. So, when we get to the fifth day, we've done a lot of work with that as well. And Ricks has kept to really good spinners before as well (like to) Rashid Khan. He's kept to everyone. So the bowlers he will keep to are familiar to him. I'm confident he will do a good job, he added. Van Wyk added that the extra responsibility of wearing the gloves should prove beneficial for Rickelton's overall focus and leadership on the field. The batter had scored 0 and 2 in South Africa's defeat in Durban. With regard to managing energies, resources and concentration, I think it's going to be really good for Ricks to have the gloves, he said. It engages him in the game even more. He's someone who thrives with extra responsibility. Having the gloves is going to be good for his game overall. He's a natural leader as well. So I've got no worries about his tank being too small and him not being able to switch from keeping to batting. He's been doing it for years anyway. He'll be fine, he added. Addressing the external pressure on the team after the series opener, van Wyk maintained that the players are simply focused on executing their roles under the spotlight. Everyone wants to do well. It's not a case of when you have to do well, it becomes a problem, van Wyk said. It's nothing different from what you normally face in an international sport. The second Test gets underway in Gqeberha, where South Africa will look to level the series and gain ground in the World Test Championship standings. (ANI)

article.headline: Proteas Bring Back Rabada and Restructure Wicketkeeping for Must-Win Gqeberha Test
article.summary: South Africa reshuffles its XI to include Kagiso Rabada and Ryan Rickelton for Sunday's second Test in Gqeberha after a 214-run series-opening loss to Australia.
article.body:
South Africa enters Sunday’s second Test in Gqeberha looking to bridge a 214-run gap from the opening defeat in Durban, where Australia cruised to victory after setting a massive target of 421. Matt Renshaw dominated that opener for the visitors with scores of 190 and 82, while Josh Hazlewood dismantled the Proteas’ lineup with six wickets for 49 runs to leave the hosts scrambling to keep their series hopes alive.

This match holds high stakes for the World Test Championship standings, as Australia currently paces the field with an 81.82% points percentage. Defending champions South Africa sit third at 60%, making this contest a critical step toward securing a final appearance for the 2025-27 cycle.

To counter Australia’s momentum, the Proteas are calling on pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada to return from a hamstring injury. The team is also handing wicketkeeping duties to Ryan Rickelton, a move fielding coach Kruger van Wyk says will help the batter thrive through extra responsibility. Rickelton, who replaces Kyle Verreynne behind the stumps, has maintained his technical training despite recent batting-only roles in international cricket.

Australia is expected to retain their winning XI, though Cameron Green remains under an injury cloud. Play begins at 10:00 a.m. local time on October 18 at St George’s Park, with live coverage provided by the Eurosport TV Network and the FanCode app in India.

article.headline: Leeds eye first consecutive league wins over Manchester United in 54 years
article.summary: Leeds United host Manchester United at Elland Road this Sunday at 2pm with a chance to secure back-to-back league victories against their rivals for the first time since 1972.
article.body:
Leeds United have not secured consecutive league victories over Manchester United since the 1971/72 campaign, but Sunday offers an opportunity to break that 54-year wait. The club enters the clash sitting eighth in the Premier League table, marking the first time since September 2002 that they have hosted this specific fixture while ranked above their visitors, who currently sit in 14th place.

This matchup carries significant weight for the hosts, who are looking to capitalize on their strong home form to maintain their position in the standings. A win would not only provide three points but also serve as a definitive statement regarding their progress this season under Daniel Farke. For fans, the fixture represents the latest chapter in one of English football’s fiercest rivalries, intensified by the home side's current standing relative to their opponents.

According to the official Leeds United website, the Whites are currently on an unbeaten run of seven Premier League home games, including four wins and three draws. Daniel Farke’s team successfully snapped a 10-game winless streak against Manchester United in April with a 2-1 victory at Old Trafford, where Noah Okafor scored twice. Defensively, Leeds have proven resilient at Elland Road, conceding only twice across three home matches this season and keeping clean sheets in four of their last seven home fixtures. They have also avoided conceding more than one goal in any of their last 10 home league games.

Following the 2pm kick-off on Sunday, Leeds will look to continue their unbeaten home streak, which stands as their longest since a 15-game run between January and December 2001. The team aims to utilize the Elland Road crowd to build on the momentum gained from their recent victory at Old Trafford.

article.headline: Lionel Messi scores twice as Inter Miami routs Atlanta United 3-1
article.summary: Lionel Messi recorded two second-half goals and one assist to lead Inter Miami to a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United on Saturday night.
article.body:
Lionel Messi set a new league milestone by becoming the first player in MLS history to record at least 15 assists in three consecutive seasons. His efforts on Saturday night pushed his season tally to 25 goals and 15 assists, leaving him only nine goal contributions shy of Carlos Vela’s 2019 single-season record. With four matches left in the regular season, the Miami star is rapidly closing in on that historic benchmark.

This victory maintains momentum for Inter Miami as they compete in the final stretch of the season. For Atlanta United, the result highlights a difficult defensive outing despite Lucas Hoyos making two saves throughout the match. The outcome impacts the standings as both clubs prepare for their respective challenges in the final weeks of league play.

The scoring opened in the final minute of the first half when Germán Berterame converted an assist from Messi and Luis Suárez to claim his ninth goal of the season. Messi then dominated the 56th and 60th minutes, scoring twice to secure a 3-0 lead. While Dayne St. Clair was denied a clean sheet after Fafà Picault converted a penalty kick in the 89th minute, Miami’s lead remained unchallenged. According to Marca, Messi is now tied for the league lead in assists and continues to pursue the single-season goal contribution record.

Looking ahead, both teams return to the pitch this coming Saturday. Atlanta United is scheduled to host the Chicago Fire, while Inter Miami will travel to face the New York Red Bulls.

article.headline: Johan Manzambi Snatches Winner As Aston Villa Downs Struggling Newcastle United
article.summary: Johan Manzambi scored the decisive goal in a 1-0 victory for Aston Villa against Newcastle United on Saturday.
article.body:
Johan Manzambi marked his 21st birthday week by scoring his third goal in Aston Villa colors, heading home the winner from eight yards out after an excellent cross from Joao Gomes. The midfielder, who was heavily linked to a move to St James' Park before completing a club-record deal exceeding £50m at Villa Park, proved his quality to the home crowd in a result that left Newcastle fans voicing their frustration with audible boos at the final whistle. Manzambi previously contributed to a 3-2 victory over Tottenham and a 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce in the Champions League, cementing his status as a key part of Unai Emery’s current rebuild.

The defeat underscores recent difficulties for Newcastle, as the home side struggled to create chances throughout the afternoon. According to Sky Sports reporter Keith Downie, the host performance appeared tepid, with the team frequently overrun and outnumbered in the middle of the pitch. Manager Unai Emery praised Manzambi’s intelligence, physicality, and defensive work rate, noting that the player's immediate impact has been vital for the squad's offensive and defensive setups.

For Newcastle, the afternoon ended with a late, unsuccessful tactical shift that saw defender Dan Burn moved into an attacking role to chase an equalizer. The loss highlights ongoing challenges for the club as they look to address midfield vulnerabilities, while Villa continues to find form under Emery’s guidance. Manzambi, who previously helped Freiburg reach the Europa League final, remains in the spotlight as a nominee for the Kopa Trophy, awarded to the best player in the world under the age of 21.

Previously marked by an unwanted record as the first team in Liga MX history to lose their opening eight matchdays, the visitors arrived in Mexico City hoping to build on isolated positive results against Tigres and Tijuana. However, those performances occurred exclusively at their home ground, and they were unable to contain Cruz Azul's surging attack throughout the match.

With this outcome, Cruz Azul solidifies its position among the league's top sides, while FC Juarez remains at the lower end of the table. The victory provides a necessary cushion for the hosts as they look to maintain their form and secure a favorable seeding heading into the postseason phase of the competition.

article.headline: Sonay Kartal Stuns Ostapenko To Clinch Historic First WTA 1,000 Career Final
article.summary: British tennis player Sonay Kartal reaches her first WTA 1,000 final at the Wuhan Open after defeating Jelena Ostapenko in straight sets.
article.body:
Sonay Kartal survived six set points across two tense tie-breaks, clawing back from 4-1 deficits in both sets to topple Jelena Ostapenko 7-6, 7-6. The 24-year-old is now the lowest-ranked player at world number 170 to reach a WTA 1,000 final since the tournament format began in 1990.

This performance marks a meteoric rise for the British athlete, who spent six months sidelined with a back injury earlier this year. The victory ensures Kartal will return to the world's top 50 rankings and become the British number one player when the official list is updated on Monday. For tennis followers, her rapid return to form signals a significant shift in the competitive landscape as she prepares for the biggest match of her professional career.

Kartal’s journey to the final has been defined by extreme tenacity. In addition to defeating the former Grand Slam champion Ostapenko, she secured notable victories over world number 6 Elina Svitolina, Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, and Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini. The BBC reports that the victory over Ostapenko was one of the toughest matches of her career, with Kartal acknowledging the mental strain of riding the momentum against such high-caliber opponents.

Kartal will face Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open final this Sunday. Having already surprised herself with how quickly her game has returned, Kartal remains focused on maintaining her current level as she looks toward the remainder of the season.

article.headline: Munster storms to Champions Cup victory in emotional tribute to Anthony Foley
article.summary: Munster secured a 33-25 win over Racing 92 at Páirc Uí Chaoimh to kick off their Investec Champions Cup campaign.
article.body:
Youngster Brian Gleeson epitomized the spirit of the evening, wearing the number 24 jersey to score the opening try in memory of the late Anthony Foley, a decade after his passing. Playing with the intensity of an emotional grudge match, Munster maintained their 100% record at the Cork venue as 24,906 spectators watched them clinch a five-try win. While Racing 92 struck first through an early Antoine Gibert penalty, the hosts quickly regained control, with Shay McCarthy adding a spectacular 40-plus metre score to extend the lead.

For the Munster squad, the victory served as a significant opening statement in their European campaign, even if the performance was marked by occasional turnovers and inconsistent kicking. The match carried immense weight, with the home side honoring the legacy of their former coach and number eight by retiring that jersey for the night. The occasion was further defined by communal tributes, including a rendition of the Shannon RFC anthem and a moment of silence for Lions player Hyron Andrews, who recently passed away.

According to RTE, the winning effort featured scores from Gleeson, McCarthy, Tadhg Beirne, Fineen Wycherley, and Player of the Match Craig Casey. The Irish Times noted that while the team played in fits and starts, their set-pieces remained reliable, supported by strong contributions from Marnus van der Merwe. Racing 92 kept the pressure on throughout the encounter, but they were unable to overcome the gap created by Munster's clinical strike plays and late-game surges. This victory ensures Munster begins their season on positive terms, building momentum as they look ahead to the remainder of the tournament.
